The Apple identify function is the vulnerable one. It calls `strcmp((const char *) e->data, "Apple iOS")` without checking that `e->size` is large enough. `strcmp` reads until it finds a NUL byte. If `e->data` is not NUL-terminated within the buffer, `strcmp` will read out of bounds.

This is a classic out-of-bounds read. The `e->data` buffer is `e->size` bytes, and if it doesn't contain a NUL byte, `strcmp` reads past the end of the buffer.

Let me understand how the identify functions are called and how the data flows. Let me look at exif-data.c around line 799.
